summaries.summary: Message passing over graphs and GNNs have long existed, but GNNs were recently investigated with deep learning, including spectral approaches linked to MP.
The MP framework recursively aggregates neighborhoods, updating each vertex representation from neighbor messages, and describes all spectral GNNs.
The paper proposes MPAD and hierarchical variants for document understanding using word co-occurrence networks, competitive on 10 document classification datasets.
The paper outlines background on MP, MPAD, the experimental framework, results, and relevant literature in subsequent sections.
BIBREF13 proposed an MP framework reformulating many recent GNNs, with aggregation followed by combination and messages computed from neighbors.
The new representation of v combines its current feature vector with the message vector.
Messages pass for T time steps through different layers, making final features capture T-height subtree topology and vertex representation distributions.
For graph-level feature vectors, a permutation-invariant READOUT pooling function is applied.
The authors next present the MP network developed for document understanding.
Documents are represented as directed weighted statistical word co-occurrence networks using a sliding window of size 2 overspanning sentences.
G compactly represents documents, with immediate neighbors as consecutive words, length 2 paths as bigrams, and longer paths as n-grams or relaxed n-grams.
G includes a special document node linked to all other nodes via unit weight bi-directional edges, and n includes the master node.
The authors formulate their AGGREGATE function.
H^t contains node features, A is asymmetric with zero diagonal, D is the in-degree matrix, MLP is a multi-layer perceptron, and M^{t+1} is the message matrix.
An MLP is used because 1-layer perceptrons are inferior for graph classification and are not universal approximators of multiset functions, with a different MLP at each layer.
Renormalization uses in-degrees to average incoming neighbor features, losing injectivity in special cases but outperforming summing in an ablation experiment.
The COMBINE function uses the Gated Recurrent Unit.
Biases are omitted for readability.
Trainable W and U matrices are not shared across time steps, while reset and update gates control previous information and interpolation toward new representations.
GRU updates should let nodes encode local and global signals by remembering past iterations, and all iteration representations are considered during readout.
After T iterations, H^T contains final vertex representations, and G without the special document node has representation matrix Hhat^T.
READOUT concatenates self-attention over Hhat^T with the final document node representation, using global self-attention to compute attentional vector u^T.
Using multiple context vectors with V^T instead of v^T gave unconvincing results, even with a diversity regularization term.
The master node representation bypasses attention via a skip connection, injecting expected global document information into h_G^T.
Multi-readout applies readout to all time steps and concatenates results, following recommendations to retain earlier, more local representations.
This modification accounts for features aggregated from subtrees of heights from 1 to T, corresponding to local and global features.
MPAD may implicitly capture document hierarchy, but the authors propose hierarchical variants representing each sentence as a word co-occurrence network embedded by MPAD.
MPAD-sentence-att combines sentence embeddings through self-attention.
MPAD-clique builds a complete graph of sentence nodes and feeds it to MPAD initialized with sentence embeddings.
MPAD-path builds a path graph linking consecutive sentences with directed edges according to natural text flow.
MPAD document embeddings are evaluated on 10 document classification datasets spanning topic identification, sentiment analysis, opinion mining, and subjectivity detection.
Reuters contains 1987 Reuters news agency stories, using the ModApte split, the 10 largest classes, and removing multi-class documents and 2 empty classes.
BBCSport contains documents from the BBC Sport website corresponding to 2004-2005 sports news articles.
Polarity features positive and negative labeled snippets from Rotten Tomatoes.
Subjectivity contains Rotten Tomatoes subjective movie review snippets and Internet Movie Database objective plot summaries.
MPQA consists of positive and negative phrases annotated during the summer 2002 NRRC Workshop on Multi-Perspective Question Answering.
IMDB is a collection of highly polarized positive and negative IMDB movie reviews, with at most 30 reviews for each movie.
TREC consists of questions classified into 6 different categories.
SST-1 uses the same snippets as Polarity, parsed and split into sentences, with phrases annotated by Amazon Mechanical Turk into five polarity classes.
SST-2 is the same as SST-1 but removes neutral reviews and classifies snippets as positive or negative.
Yelp2013 features reviews obtained from the 2013 Yelp Dataset Challenge.
MPAD is evaluated against multiple state-of-the-art baseline models, including hierarchical ones for fair comparison with hierarchical MPAD variants.
doc2vec learns document vectors fully unsupervised and feeds document embeddings to a logistic regression classifier.
CNN applies a convolutional neural network architecture to text with one spatial dimension and word embeddings as channels.
DAN passes the unweighted average of input word embeddings through multiple dense layers and a final softmax.
Tree-LSTM generalizes the standard LSTM architecture to constituency and dependency parse trees.
DRNN stacks recursive neural networks and applies them to parse trees.
LSTMN extends LSTM by replacing the memory cell with a memory network storing word representations.
C-LSTM combines convolutional and recurrent neural networks by feeding CNN region embeddings to a LSTM.
SPGK models documents as word co-occurrence networks, computes a shortest-path graph kernel, and uses a SVM to categorize documents.
WMD applies Earth Mover's Distance to text and uses a k-nearest neighbor classifier.
S-WMD is a supervised extension of the Word Mover's Distance.
Semantic-CNN applies a CNN to semantic units obtained by clustering words in the embedding space.
LSTM-GRNN is hierarchical, obtaining sentence embeddings with a CNN and feeding sentence representations to a GRU-RNN for a document vector.
HN-ATT is hierarchical, using a bidirectional GRU-RNN for sentences and documents with different parameters and self-attention at each level.
All datasets are preprocessed with BIBREF38 code, Yelp2013 replaces tokens appearing strictly less than 6 times with UNK, and directed word co-occurrence networks use a window of size 2.
Basic MPAD uses T=2, hierarchical variants use two MP iterations per level, d is 64 except d=128 on IMDB and Yelp, and training uses Adam with learning rate 0.001.
Batch normalization follows the skip connection, dropout has rate 0.5, the best epoch is capped at 200, and cross-validation uses 10% of each fold's training set.
All datasets except Yelp2013 initialize H^0 with publicly available 300-dimensional pre-trained Google News vectors, while Yelp2013 learns word vectors with gensim word2vec.
MPAD was implemented in Python 3.6 with PyTorch and run on a 3.4 GHz Intel Core i7 CPU, 16 GB of RAM, and an NVidia GeForce Titan Xp GPU.
Table TABREF28 shows MPAD reaches best performance on 7 out of 10 datasets and close second elsewhere across varied settings.
On 9 datasets out of 10, one or more hierarchical variants outperform vanilla MPAD, highlighting benefits of modeling document hierarchy.
Standard MPAD outperforms hierarchical variants on Subjectivity and matches accuracy on TREC, possibly due to cross-sentence context in single document graphs.
Additional hyperparameter experiments on Reuters, Polarity, and IMDB used non-hierarchical MPAD, with results in Table TABREF29.
Varying message passing iterations from 1 to 4 shows more iterations improve performance, attributed to readout from each iteration from 1 to $T$.
Undirected edges improve Reuters performance but hurt Polarity and IMDB, explained by topic classification versus sentiment analysis and word order.
Removing the master node deteriorates performance across all datasets, showing its value for encoding a document summary during message passing.
Using sum instead of mean without renormalization decreases performance everywhere, suggesting neighbor representation distributions matter more than structure.
Replacing the GRU combine function with identity makes updates neighbors-only, hurting performance except on Reuters and stressing root node importance.
The following brief review covers relevant studies ranked by increasing similarity with this work.
BIBREF9, BIBREF54, BIBREF11, and BIBREF10 run node classification on citation networks where text only provides node features.
BIBREF55 and BIBREF7 use $k$-nearest neighbor similarity graphs for document classification, with BIBREF7 representing each document as a graph.
BIBREF56 uses a GNN for hierarchical classification into a large taxonomy of topics with word co-occurrence networks and word embeddings.
BIBREF53 builds one undirected word-document graph with TF-IDF and pointwise mutual information weights for semi-supervised node classification.
MPAD differs from BIBREF53 by being inductive, using directed graphs, losing corpus-level dependencies, and avoiding vocabulary-size-dependent PMI computation.
MPAD applies message passing to NLP, performs competitively on 10 standard text classification datasets, and includes three improved hierarchical variants.
The authors thank the NVidia corporation for donating a GPU through their GPU grant program.
